courses.title: Management and Organisational Behaviour, MBA Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Evolution of management thought
topics.summary: Classical, neo-classical, systems and contingency theories.
notes: Classical: Taylor (scientific management), Fayol (administrative principles), Weber (bureaucracy).
Neo-classical: Hawthorne studies, human relations, McGregor's Theory X and Y.
Systems theory views the organisation as an open system of interrelated parts; contingency theory says the best approach depends on the situation.
Drucker emphasised management by objectives and knowledge workers.
outcomes: Trace the evolution of management thought
Apply contingency thinking to a case

topics.title: Personality, perception and attitudes
topics.summary: Personality theories, attribution and job attitudes.
notes: Big Five and MBTI are common personality frameworks.
Attribution theory: behaviour is judged as internally or externally caused using distinctiveness, consensus and consistency; the fundamental attribution error overweights internal causes.
Job satisfaction, organisational commitment and engagement predict performance and turnover.
outcomes: Use attribution theory to explain judgements of others

topics.title: Motivation theories
topics.summary: Content and process theories of motivation.
notes: Content: Maslow, Herzberg's two-factor theory, McClelland's needs for achievement, affiliation and power, Alderfer's ERG.
Process: Vroom's expectancy (M = E × I × V), Adams' equity theory, Locke's goal-setting theory.
Goal-setting: specific, difficult goals with feedback lead to higher performance.
outcomes: Design a motivation scheme for a team

topics.title: Leadership theories
topics.summary: Trait, behavioural, contingency and transformational leadership.
notes: Behavioural studies: Ohio State (initiating structure, consideration), Michigan (employee- vs production-oriented), Blake and Mouton's managerial grid.
Fiedler's contingency model matches style (LPC) to situational favourableness; Hersey–Blanchard matches style to follower readiness.
Transformational leaders inspire and change followers; transactional leaders exchange rewards for performance.
outcomes: Choose a leadership style for a situation

topics.title: Culture, power and change
topics.summary: Organisational culture, power and politics, and change management.
notes: Schein's levels of culture: artefacts, espoused values, basic assumptions.
French and Raven's bases of power: legitimate, reward, coercive, expert, referent.
Kotter's eight steps to lead change begin with creating urgency and end with anchoring changes in culture.

courses.title: Managerial Economics, MBA Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Demand analysis and elasticity
topics.summary: Demand functions, elasticities and their managerial use.
notes: Point price elasticity e = (dQ/dP) × (P/Q); arc elasticity uses average P and Q.
Total revenue is maximised where price elasticity equals −1 (MR = 0).
MR = P(1 + 1/e), linking pricing to elasticity.
Advertising and income elasticity guide promotion and market expansion.
outcomes: Relate elasticity to marginal revenue and pricing

lesson.hook: A cinema raises ticket prices and earns less. What did it not know about its customers?
lesson.example:
Q = 100 − 2P. At P = 20, Q = 60; e = −2 × 20 ÷ 60 = −0.67 (inelastic): raising price raises revenue.
Revenue is maximum where e = −1: P = 25, Q = 50, TR = ₹1,250.

questions.q: If e = −2 and P = ₹100, what is MR?

topics.title: Demand forecasting
topics.summary: Survey and statistical methods of forecasting demand.
notes: Survey methods: buyers' intentions, expert opinion (Delphi), sales force composite.
Statistical methods: trend projection, moving averages, exponential smoothing, regression.
Exponential smoothing: Fₜ₊₁ = αAₜ + (1 − α)Fₜ.

topics.title: Production and cost functions
topics.summary: Cobb–Douglas production, economies of scale and cost curves.
notes: Cobb–Douglas: Q = A Lᵅ Kᵝ; α + β > 1, = 1 or < 1 gives increasing, constant or decreasing returns to scale.
Least-cost combination: MPL ÷ w = MPK ÷ r.
Long-run average cost is the envelope of short-run curves; economies of scale lower it.
outcomes: Identify returns to scale from a production function

topics.title: Pricing under market structures
topics.summary: Equilibrium in competitive, monopoly and oligopoly markets, and pricing practices.
notes: Profit maximisation: MR = MC.
A monopolist with constant MC charges P = MC ÷ (1 + 1/e).
Oligopoly models: Cournot (quantity), Bertrand (price), kinked demand; game theory and the prisoners' dilemma.
Pricing practices: cost-plus, peak-load, transfer pricing, price discrimination.
outcomes: Find the profit-maximising price and output
Analyse a duopoly as a game

topics.title: National income, inflation and policy
topics.summary: GDP, business cycles, and monetary and fiscal policy.
notes: GDP = C + I + G + (X − M).
Monetary policy (RBI): repo rate, CRR, SLR, open market operations; fiscal policy: taxes and government spending.
The multiplier = 1 ÷ (1 − MPC).
outcomes: Explain the effect of policy on business

courses.title: Accounting for Managers, MBA Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Accounting framework and standards
topics.summary: Concepts, the accounting cycle and Ind AS.
notes: Accounting cycle: transactions, journal, ledger, trial balance, adjustments, financial statements.
Accrual basis records revenue when earned and expenses when incurred.
Ind AS are converged with IFRS; the Conceptual Framework defines assets, liabilities, equity, income and expenses.

topics.title: Reading financial statements
topics.summary: Balance sheet, statement of profit and loss and cash flow statement.
notes: The balance sheet shows financial position at a date; the statement of profit and loss shows performance over a period.
Cash flow statement (Ind AS 7) separates operating, investing and financing cash flows.
Profit is not cash: depreciation, credit sales and working capital changes cause differences.
outcomes: Reconcile profit with operating cash flow

topics.title: Ratio and DuPont analysis
topics.summary: Liquidity, solvency, efficiency and profitability ratios, and the DuPont identity.
notes: ROE = Net profit ÷ Equity.
DuPont: ROE = Net profit margin × Asset turnover × Equity multiplier (Assets ÷ Equity).
Interest coverage = EBIT ÷ Interest.
Compare ratios over time (trend) and with peers (cross-section).

lesson.hook: Two companies both earn 20% ROE. One is a supermarket, the other a luxury brand. How can that be?
lesson.example:
Supermarket: margin 2%, turnover 5, equity multiplier 2: ROE = 0.02 × 5 × 2 = 20%.
Luxury brand: margin 20%, turnover 0.5, multiplier 2: ROE = 20%.

questions.q: Net profit ₹10 lakh, sales ₹100 lakh, assets ₹50 lakh, equity ₹25 lakh. ROE by DuPont?

topics.title: Cost behaviour and CVP
topics.summary: Fixed and variable costs, contribution and break-even analysis.
notes: Contribution margin ratio = Contribution ÷ Sales.
Break-even sales = Fixed costs ÷ CM ratio; margin of safety = (Actual − BE sales) ÷ Actual sales.
Operating leverage = Contribution ÷ Operating profit.
outcomes: Do a break-even and target-profit analysis

topics.title: Budgeting and variance analysis
topics.summary: Master budget, flexible budget and standard costing variances.
notes: Master budget: sales, production, cost and cash budgets leading to budgeted statements.
Flexible budget variance compares actual with a budget flexed to actual activity.
Material price variance = AQ(SP − AP); usage variance = SP(SQ − AQ).

courses.title: Statistics for Management, MBA Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Summarising data
topics.summary: Central tendency, dispersion and shape.
notes: Mean, median and mode; weighted mean = Σwx ÷ Σw.
Standard deviation and coefficient of variation; z-score = (x − μ) ÷ σ.
Skewness and kurtosis describe shape; box plots show quartiles and outliers (beyond 1.5 × IQR).
outcomes: Summarise a dataset numerically and graphically

topics.title: Probability and Bayes' theorem
topics.summary: Rules of probability, conditional probability and Bayes' theorem.
notes: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B); P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) ÷ P(B).
Bayes: P(A | B) = P(B | A) P(A) ÷ P(B).
Independent events: P(A ∩ B) = P(A) P(B).
outcomes: Apply conditional probability to business cases

lesson.hook: A test is 95% accurate and 1% of products are defective. If the test flags a product, how likely is it really defective?

questions.q: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, independent. P(A and B)?

topics.title: Binomial, Poisson and normal
topics.summary: Discrete and continuous distributions for business problems.
notes: Binomial: mean np, variance np(1 − p); Poisson: mean = variance = λ.
Poisson approximates the binomial when n is large and p small (λ = np).
outcomes: Compute binomial, Poisson and normal probabilities

topics.title: Sampling distributions and confidence intervals
topics.summary: Central limit theorem, standard error and interval estimates.
notes: Central limit theorem: for large n, the sample mean is approximately normal with mean μ and standard error σ ÷ √n.
95% confidence interval for μ: x̄ ± 1.96 σ ÷ √n (use t with n − 1 df when σ is unknown and n small).
Sample size for a mean: n = (zσ ÷ E)².

topics.title: Tests and simple regression
topics.summary: z, t, chi-square and ANOVA tests, and regression analysis.
notes: Steps: state H₀ and H₁, choose α, compute the test statistic, compare with the critical value or use the p-value.
One-way ANOVA: F = MS between ÷ MS within.
Least squares: b = Σ(x − x̄)(y − ȳ) ÷ Σ(x − x̄)²; R² is the share of variation explained.
outcomes: Fit and interpret a regression model

courses.title: Legal Environment of Business, MBA Semester 1
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Indian Contract Act, 1872
topics.summary: Essentials of a valid contract, void and voidable agreements, and remedies.
notes: A contract is an agreement enforceable by law (section 2(h)); essentials: offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity, free consent, lawful object, not expressly void.
A minor's agreement is void (Mohori Bibee v Dharmodas Ghose).
Consent caused by coercion, undue influence, fraud or misrepresentation makes a contract voidable.
Remedies for breach: damages (Hadley v Baxendale), specific performance, injunction, quantum meruit.
outcomes: Test the validity of a contract

chapters.title: Sale of Goods and Negotiable Instruments

topics.title: Sale of goods and negotiable instruments
topics.summary: Conditions and warranties, caveat emptor, and cheques and bills.
notes: Sale of Goods Act, 1930: a condition is essential to the contract; a warranty is collateral.
Caveat emptor (let the buyer beware) has exceptions such as fitness for purpose and merchantable quality.
Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881: promissory note, bill of exchange, cheque; section 138 makes dishonour of a cheque for insufficient funds an offence.
outcomes: Explain the consequences of cheque dishonour

topics.title: Companies Act, 2013 essentials
topics.summary: Incorporation, directors, meetings and corporate governance.
notes: Corporate social responsibility (section 135): companies above set thresholds (net worth ₹500 crore, turnover ₹1,000 crore or net profit ₹5 crore) spend 2% of average net profit.
Independent directors and audit committees strengthen governance.
NCLT handles company law matters; IBC 2016 governs insolvency resolution.

topics.title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and Competition Act, 2002
topics.summary: Consumer rights, redressal commissions and anti-competitive practices.
notes: Consumer commissions' pecuniary jurisdiction: district up to ₹50 lakh, state ₹50 lakh–₹2 crore, national above ₹2 crore (by value of goods or services paid).
The Central Consumer Protection Authority acts against unfair trade practices and misleading advertisements.
The Competition Act prohibits anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominance and regulates combinations; the CCI enforces it.

topics.title: IT Act and intellectual property
topics.summary: Electronic contracts, data protection and intellectual property rights.
notes: The IT Act, 2000 recognises electronic records and digital signatures.
The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 governs processing of personal data with consent.
IPRs: patents (20 years), trademarks (10 years, renewable), copyright (life plus 60 years for authors), designs, geographical indications.
outcomes: Explain the protection given by each IPR
State key duties under data protection law

courses.title: Financial Management, MBA Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Risk, return and CAPM
topics.summary: Measuring risk and return, diversification and the capital asset pricing model.
notes: Expected return E(R) = Σ pᵢ Rᵢ; risk is the standard deviation of returns.
Diversification removes unsystematic risk; systematic (market) risk remains, measured by beta.
CAPM: E(Rᵢ) = Rf + βᵢ(Rm − Rf).
A stock is undervalued if its expected return exceeds the CAPM required return.
outcomes: Apply CAPM to find required return

lesson.hook: Why does a power utility's share move less than the Sensex, while a tech share swings more?

questions.q: What is the required return on a stock with β = 0?

topics.title: Valuation of bonds and shares
topics.summary: Present value models for bonds and equity.
notes: Bond value = Σ C ÷ (1 + k)ᵗ + F ÷ (1 + k)ⁿ; bond prices fall when yields rise.
Gordon growth model: P₀ = D₁ ÷ (k − g), for k > g.
Yield to maturity is the discount rate equating bond price and its cash flows.

topics.title: Capital budgeting under certainty and risk
topics.summary: NPV, IRR, MIRR and risk analysis.
notes: NPV and IRR can conflict for mutually exclusive projects; NPV is preferred.
MIRR assumes reinvestment at the cost of capital.
Risk techniques: sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis, decision trees, risk-adjusted discount rate, certainty equivalents.
outcomes: Evaluate projects with NPV, IRR and MIRR

chapters.title: Cost of Capital and Capital Structure

topics.title: WACC and capital structure theories
topics.summary: Cost of each source, WACC, and NI, NOI, traditional and MM approaches.
notes: WACC = Σ wᵢkᵢ, using market value weights where possible.
MM without taxes: firm value is independent of capital structure; with taxes, V_L = V_U + tD.
Trade-off theory balances tax shields against financial distress costs; pecking order prefers internal funds, then debt, then equity.

topics.title: Dividend policy and working capital management
topics.summary: Dividend models, and managing cash, receivables and inventory.
notes: Walter: if r > k retain all earnings; if r < k pay out all.
MM dividend irrelevance holds in perfect markets.
Receivables policy weighs extra contribution from credit sales against the cost of funds and bad debts.
Cash conversion cycle = Inventory days + Receivable days − Payable days.

courses.title: Marketing Management, MBA Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Marketing and value creation
topics.summary: Marketing concept, value delivery and strategic planning.
notes: Value proposition: the set of benefits promised to customers.
Marketing plan: situation analysis, objectives, strategy (STP and mix), action programmes, budgets, controls.
Customer equity is the total lifetime value of all customers.

topics.title: Consumer and business buying behaviour
topics.summary: Buying decision process and organisational buying.
notes: Consumer decision process: problem recognition, search, evaluation, decision, post-purchase (cognitive dissonance).
Business buying centre roles: initiators, users, influencers, deciders, approvers, buyers, gatekeepers.
Buy classes: straight rebuy, modified rebuy, new task.
outcomes: Identify roles in a buying centre

topics.title: Brand equity and product strategy
topics.summary: Brand elements, brand equity models and product line decisions.
notes: Keller's customer-based brand equity pyramid: salience, performance and imagery, judgements and feelings, resonance.
Brand strategies: line extension, brand extension, multibrands, new brands.
Product line decisions: stretching (up, down) and filling.
outcomes: Analyse a brand with Keller's pyramid
Recommend brand and product line strategies

topics.title: Pricing strategy and channel management
topics.summary: Pricing objectives and methods, channel conflict and omnichannel retail.
notes: Price elasticity, costs and competitors' prices set the pricing range.
Channel conflict may be vertical, horizontal or multichannel.
Omnichannel retail integrates stores, online and mobile into one customer experience.
outcomes: Set a price using value and cost

topics.title: Integrated communications and digital marketing
topics.summary: Communication process, media planning and digital channels.
notes: Media planning: reach, frequency, GRP = Reach × Frequency.
Digital funnel metrics: impressions, CTR, conversion rate, CAC, ROAS = Revenue ÷ Ad spend.
Content, social, search and influencer marketing build owned, earned and paid media.
outcomes: Evaluate a digital campaign with funnel metrics

courses.title: Human Resource Management, MBA Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: HR strategy and planning
topics.summary: Linking HR with strategy, HR planning and HR analytics.
notes: Best-fit vs best-practice approaches to HRM.
Workforce planning forecasts demand and supply (Markov analysis, trend analysis).
HR analytics uses data on hiring, performance and attrition to make decisions.
outcomes: Align HR plans with business strategy

topics.title: Recruitment, selection and onboarding
topics.summary: Employer branding, selection methods and induction.
notes: Employer branding attracts candidates by communicating the employee value proposition.
Structured interviews and work-sample tests have higher validity than unstructured interviews.
Onboarding integrates new hires and reduces early attrition.
outcomes: Design a selection process with valid tools

topics.title: Training and talent management
topics.summary: Training cycle, evaluation and talent pipelines.
notes: Training cycle: needs analysis, design, delivery, evaluation (Kirkpatrick's four levels; Phillips adds ROI).
Talent management identifies high potentials (9-box grid) and plans succession.
Competency mapping defines the knowledge, skills and behaviours for each role.

topics.title: Performance management and reward
topics.summary: Performance management systems, pay structures and incentives.
notes: Performance management sets goals (OKRs or KPIs), gives continuous feedback and reviews.
Pay structure is built from job evaluation and market surveys; compa-ratio = Actual pay ÷ Midpoint of range.
Variable pay links reward to individual, team or company performance.

topics.title: Industrial relations and labour codes
topics.summary: Unions, collective bargaining, dispute resolution and India's labour codes.
notes: Dispute resolution: negotiation, conciliation, arbitration, adjudication.
The four labour codes: Code on Wages, 2019; Industrial Relations Code, 2020; Code on Social Security, 2020; Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020.
Grievance redressal committees resolve individual complaints.
outcomes: Name the four labour codes and their scope

courses.title: Quantitative Techniques and Operations Research, MBA Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Formulation and graphical solution
topics.summary: Formulating LP models and solving two-variable problems graphically.
notes: An LP has decision variables, a linear objective, linear constraints and non-negativity.
The optimum of a bounded feasible LP lies at a corner point.
Special cases: unbounded, infeasible, multiple optima, redundant constraints.

lesson.hook: A furniture maker has 240 carpentry hours and 100 painting hours. How many tables and chairs make the most profit?
lesson.example:
Tables (₹70 profit) need 4 h carpentry and 2 h painting; chairs (₹50) 3 h and 1 h. Max Z = 70x + 50y.
4x + 3y ≤ 240, 2x + y ≤ 100. Corners: (0,0), (50,0), (30,40), (0,80). Z = 0; 3,500; 4,100; 4,000. Best: 30 tables, 40 chairs.

questions.a: A linear objective reaches its optimum at a vertex of the feasible region.

topics.title: Simplex method and duality
topics.summary: Standard form, simplex iterations and the dual problem.
notes: Slack variables convert ≤ constraints into equations; surplus and artificial variables handle ≥ constraints (Big-M or two-phase).
The entering variable has the most negative Cj − Zj (maximisation); the leaving variable has the minimum ratio.
Every LP has a dual; shadow prices give the value of one more unit of a resource.
outcomes: Solve an LP by the simplex method

topics.title: Transportation and assignment problems
topics.summary: Initial solutions, optimality test and the Hungarian method.
notes: Initial basic feasible solution: north-west corner, least cost, Vogel's approximation method.
Optimality: MODI (u–v) method; a solution needs m + n − 1 occupied cells.
Assignment: Hungarian method (row and column reduction, cover zeros with minimum lines).
outcomes: Solve a transportation problem with VAM and MODI

topics.title: Decision making under uncertainty and game theory
topics.summary: Maximin, maximax, regret and expected value criteria, and two-person zero-sum games.
notes: Under risk, choose the act with the highest expected monetary value; EVPI = expected value with perfect information − best EMV.
Under uncertainty: maximin (pessimist), maximax (optimist), minimax regret, Hurwicz, Laplace.
A game has a saddle point when maximin = minimax; otherwise use mixed strategies.
outcomes: Apply decision criteria to a payoff table

topics.title: PERT, CPM and queuing
topics.summary: Critical path, project duration and basic queuing models.
notes: The critical path is the longest path; its activities have zero float.
PERT expected time tₑ = (a + 4m + b) ÷ 6; variance = ((b − a) ÷ 6)².
M/M/1 queue: utilisation ρ = λ ÷ μ; average number in the system L = λ ÷ (μ − λ).
outcomes: Find the critical path and project duration

courses.title: Research Methodology, MBA Semester 2
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2024-25)

topics.title: Research process and design
topics.summary: Types of research, problem formulation and research designs.
notes: Research designs: exploratory, descriptive (cross-sectional, longitudinal), causal (experiments).
A good research problem is specific, researchable and significant.
Validity: internal (cause and effect) and external (generalisability).

topics.title: Measurement, scales and reliability
topics.summary: Levels of measurement, attitude scales and reliability.
notes: Levels: nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio.
Attitude scales: Likert, semantic differential, Thurstone.
Cronbach's alpha above about 0.7 indicates acceptable internal consistency.

topics.title: Sampling design and fieldwork
topics.summary: Sampling frames, techniques and sample size.
notes: Probability sampling allows estimates of sampling error.
Sample size for a proportion: n = z² p(1 − p) ÷ e².
Data collection: surveys (online, telephone, personal), observation, interviews, focus groups.

topics.title: Multivariate analysis basics
topics.summary: Univariate tests and an overview of multivariate techniques.
notes: Parametric tests (t, ANOVA) assume normality; non-parametric alternatives include Mann–Whitney and Kruskal–Wallis.
Multiple regression: Y = b₀ + b₁X₁ + … + bₖXₖ; check multicollinearity (VIF).
Factor analysis reduces variables; cluster analysis groups cases; discriminant analysis classifies them.

topics.title: Research report and ethics
topics.summary: Writing the report and ethical research.
notes: Report structure: executive summary, introduction, methodology, findings, limitations, recommendations.
Ethics: informed consent, confidentiality, no harm, honest reporting.
Plagiarism checks and proper citation are required for academic work.

courses.title: Strategic Management, MBA Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Vision, mission and strategic intent
topics.summary: Strategic intent, stakeholders and corporate governance.
notes: Strategic intent (Hamel and Prahalad) is an ambitious goal that stretches the organisation.
Stakeholder mapping uses power and interest.
Good governance aligns management with shareholders and other stakeholders.
outcomes: Map stakeholders by power and interest

topics.title: External analysis and core competencies
topics.summary: PESTEL, five forces, resource-based view and VRIO.
notes: PESTEL scans the macro environment; Porter's five forces analyse industry attractiveness.
Resource-based view: sustainable advantage comes from valuable, rare, inimitable resources.
VRIO: valuable, rare, inimitable, organised to exploit.
outcomes: Analyse an industry with five forces
Apply VRIO to a firm's resources

topics.title: Business and corporate strategy
topics.summary: Generic strategies, growth strategies and portfolio analysis.
notes: Porter's generic strategies: cost leadership, differentiation, focus; being "stuck in the middle" is risky.
Growth: concentration, integration (vertical, horizontal), diversification (related, unrelated), mergers and acquisitions, strategic alliances.
Portfolio tools: BCG matrix, GE–McKinsey nine-cell matrix.
outcomes: Choose growth strategies for a firm
Analyse a portfolio with BCG and GE matrices

topics.title: Implementing strategy
topics.summary: Structure, resource allocation, leadership and culture.
notes: Structures: functional, divisional, matrix, network.
McKinsey 7-S aligns hard and soft elements.
Blue ocean strategy creates uncontested market space (value innovation).

topics.title: Strategic control
topics.summary: Premise, implementation and strategic surveillance controls; balanced scorecard.
notes: Strategic controls: premise control, implementation control, strategic surveillance, special alert control.
Balanced scorecard links strategy to measures in four perspectives.
Strategy maps show cause-and-effect links between objectives.

courses.title: Security Analysis and Portfolio Management (Finance elective), MBA Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Investment and securities markets
topics.summary: Investment vs speculation, instruments and Indian securities markets.
notes: Investment seeks returns commensurate with risk over time; speculation seeks short-term gains at high risk.
Instruments: equity, bonds, mutual funds, derivatives, REITs and InvITs.
SEBI regulates markets; trading on NSE and BSE settles on T+1.
outcomes: Describe how securities are traded in India

topics.title: Economy, industry and company analysis
topics.summary: Top-down fundamental analysis and valuation multiples.
notes: E-I-C framework: economy, industry, company.
Industry life cycle: pioneering, expansion, stabilisation, decline.
Valuation multiples: P/E = Price ÷ EPS; P/B = Price ÷ Book value per share; EV/EBITDA.

topics.title: Technical analysis and EMH
topics.summary: Charts, indicators and the efficient market hypothesis.
notes: Dow theory: primary, secondary and minor trends.
Indicators: moving averages, RSI (above 70 overbought, below 30 oversold), MACD.
EMH forms: weak (past prices), semi-strong (public information), strong (all information).
outcomes: Read basic chart patterns and indicators
Explain the forms of market efficiency

topics.title: Markowitz and portfolio risk
topics.summary: Portfolio return and risk, diversification and the efficient frontier.
notes: Portfolio return = Σ wᵢ Rᵢ.
Two-asset risk: σp² = w₁²σ₁² + w₂²σ₂² + 2w₁w₂ρσ₁σ₂.
Diversification benefit is greatest when correlation is low or negative.
outcomes: Compute two-asset portfolio risk and return

topics.title: Performance measures
topics.summary: Sharpe, Treynor and Jensen's alpha.
notes: Sharpe ratio = (Rp − Rf) ÷ σp.
Treynor ratio = (Rp − Rf) ÷ βp.
Jensen's alpha = Rp − [Rf + βp(Rm − Rf)].
outcomes: Choose between Sharpe and Treynor measures

courses.title: Consumer Behaviour (Marketing elective), MBA Semester 3
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Consumer behaviour and research
topics.summary: Scope of consumer behaviour and consumer research.
notes: Consumer behaviour studies how people select, buy, use and dispose of products.
Research methods: surveys, ethnography, experiments, neuromarketing.
Insights guide segmentation, positioning and product design.
outcomes: Explain why marketers study consumer behaviour

topics.title: Motivation, perception and learning
topics.summary: Needs, perception, learning and memory in buying.
notes: Perception: selective exposure, attention and retention; just noticeable difference (Weber's law).
Learning: classical and operant conditioning, cognitive learning.
Involvement: high-involvement purchases involve extensive problem solving.
outcomes: Apply Weber's law to pricing and packaging

topics.title: Attitudes and personality
topics.summary: Attitude models and personality in consumption.
notes: Tri-component attitude model: cognitive, affective, conative.
Fishbein's multi-attribute model: A = Σ bᵢ eᵢ.
Brand personality (Aaker): sincerity, excitement, competence, sophistication, ruggedness.

topics.title: Reference groups, family and culture
topics.summary: Social influences on buying.
notes: Reference groups and opinion leaders shape choices; influencers act as digital opinion leaders.
Family life cycle and household decision roles affect purchases.
Culture, subculture and social class influence values and consumption.
outcomes: Analyse group influence on a purchase

topics.title: Consumer decision models
topics.summary: Decision process models and post-purchase behaviour.
notes: Models: Nicosia, Howard–Sheth, Engel–Kollat–Blackwell.
Decision rules: compensatory and non-compensatory (conjunctive, lexicographic).
Cognitive dissonance after purchase is reduced by reassurance and service.
outcomes: Apply decision rules to brand choice

courses.title: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance, MBA Semester 4
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Ethical theories and dilemmas
topics.summary: Normative theories and resolving ethical dilemmas.
notes: Theories: utilitarianism (greatest good), deontology (duty), virtue ethics, justice and rights.
An ethical dilemma is a choice between conflicting values.
Frameworks: identify facts and stakeholders, options, consequences, principles, decide and review.
outcomes: Analyse a dilemma with ethical theories

topics.title: Governance principles and mechanisms
topics.summary: Agency theory, board structure and SEBI LODR requirements.
notes: Agency theory: separation of ownership and control creates conflicts of interest.
Board committees: audit, nomination and remuneration, stakeholders' relationship, risk management.
SEBI LODR: at least half independent directors if the chair is executive (one-third if non-executive), with at least one woman independent director for the top 1,000 listed companies.
outcomes: Explain the role of board committees

topics.title: CSR and ESG
topics.summary: Section 135 CSR, ESG and sustainability reporting.
notes: CSR spending: 2% of average net profit of the last three years for qualifying companies.
ESG covers environmental, social and governance performance; BRSR is mandatory for the top 1,000 listed companies.
Triple bottom line: people, planet, profit.

topics.title: Ethics in marketing, finance and HR
topics.summary: Common ethical issues across business functions.
notes: Marketing: misleading advertising, data privacy, dark patterns.
Finance: insider trading (SEBI PIT Regulations), window dressing, conflicts of interest.
HR: discrimination, harassment (POSH Act, 2013), whistleblower protection.
outcomes: Identify ethical issues in each function

courses.title: Financial Derivatives (Finance elective), MBA Semester 4
courses.source: kinetix-curriculum-team from public BU syllabus (BU MBA CBCS, 2025-26)

topics.title: Derivatives and their markets
topics.summary: Forwards, futures, options and swaps, and their uses.
notes: A derivative's value depends on an underlying asset.
Uses: hedging, speculation, arbitrage.
Exchange-traded derivatives are standardised with a clearing house; OTC derivatives are customised and carry counterparty risk.

topics.title: Pricing and hedging with futures
topics.summary: Cost-of-carry pricing, margins and hedging.
notes: Futures price F = S × e^(rT) (cost of carry, no income); with dividend yield q, F = S × e^((r − q)T).
Futures are marked to market daily; initial and maintenance margins apply.
Hedge ratio = β × Portfolio value ÷ (Futures price × Lot size) for index futures.
outcomes: Hedge a portfolio with index futures

topics.title: Option payoffs and strategies
topics.summary: Calls, puts, payoffs and common strategies.
notes: Call payoff = max(S − K, 0); put payoff = max(K − S, 0).
Put–call parity: C + K e^(−rT) = P + S.
Strategies: covered call, protective put, straddle, strangle, bull and bear spreads.
outcomes: Choose an option strategy for a view

topics.title: Option pricing
topics.summary: Binomial model and Black–Scholes.
notes: One-step binomial: risk-neutral probability p = (e^(rT) − d) ÷ (u − d).
Black–Scholes: C = S N(d₁) − K e^(−rT) N(d₂).
Greeks: delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho.
outcomes: Value an option with a one-step binomial tree

topics.title: Interest rate and currency swaps
topics.summary: Plain vanilla swaps and their uses.
notes: An interest rate swap exchanges fixed for floating payments on a notional principal.
Comparative advantage in borrowing makes swaps beneficial to both parties.
Currency swaps exchange principal and interest in different currencies.
outcomes: Explain how a swap reduces borrowing cost
Value the cash flows of a simple swap
